title: Interference

reference.source: Reference 8: two-source ring interference artwork, 720 × 734 px JPEG
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Two ring systems whose amplitude fades with distance, added and cut hard at fixed levels into six inks whose assignment changes with distance from the sources.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 720 × 734 and every length scales with the canvas

pitch.does: Wavelength of every ring system. Sets the lozenge lattice with it.

separation.does: Distance between the sources. Closer sources make wider, flatter lozenges.

tilt.does: Rotates the line the sources sit on.

sources.does: How many ring systems beat together. One is plain rings; three or four stagger off the axis.

decay.does: How fast each wave fades with distance. 0 gives equal waves everywhere, so no source ever dominates its own neighborhood.

slip.does: Offsets the second train against the first by this phase; the lattice walks sideways.

phase.does: Position along the loop. Advances the first ring train one wavelength outward and the second 1.25, so the lattice drifts as the trains travel.

lens.does: Barrel bulge of the sheet: rings stretch toward the edges.

warp.does: Slow, uneven stretch of the sheet, so the lattice never repeats exactly and the local pitch drifts as it does in the print.

amp.does: Height of every wave against fixed cut levels. Higher pushes more of the sheet into the core inks and thins the lines between.

crest.does: Height above which a crest prints as a solid core. Lower makes fatter lenses; far out, where the waves are low, only beats reach it.

ringW.does: Depth of the band that rings each core.

trough.does: Depth below which a trough prints as its own core.

saddle.does: Half-width of the thin white line drawn where the wave crosses zero: the grid between cells and the rim of every diamond. 0 removes it.

redDuty.does: Height at which the red set switches from black to red along a wave. 0 is half the cycle close to a source.

capsBias.does: Lowers the crest cuts inside the capsule, so black cores grow into diamonds there.

near.does: The red set prints where the two ring trains run within this angle of parallel: the far side of each source and the strip between them.

gate.does: Wave strength the red set also needs, which keeps it out of the far corners.

hole.does: Flat green disc at the heart of each source.

capsule.does: Radius of the capsule around the sources where troughs print green.

wobble.does: Low-frequency wander of the zone edges so they do not read as compass circles.

spread.does: Softening of every edge, as the inks bleed a little into the sheet.

grain.does: Fine position-hashed noise on top of the inks.

seed.does: Re-rolls the zone wobble and grain.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: A source: its own rings dominate here, so the cut reads as clean red circles with thin black and blue lines.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Far to the side the two trains are equal in height: a lattice of lozenges on a 14.5 by 31 px cell, black crest cores ringed white, yellow trough cores ringed black.

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: The edge of the red reach cuts straight through lenses; the zone is a mask, not a feature of the wave.

pass_order: sources placed on a tilted axis through the plate center
per pixel: lens bulge of the coordinates, then distance to each source
each source: cosine ring train, amplitude falling as (1 + r/R)^-decay; the trains are summed, so close to a source its own train swings past every cut and far out only beats reach the core cuts

zones: eye disc at each source; red set where the two trains run within a set angle of parallel and the sum is still strong (the far side of each source and the strip between them); green capsule by distance to the axis; outside
one hard cut into seven bands (trough core, trough ring, field, saddle line, field, crest ring, crest core), each zone with its own ink set
press: equal ink spread on every edge, position-hashed grain

measured.pitch_method: autocorrelation of the radial luminance profile around each source: peaks at lags 14 and 27-28; joint fit of a two-cosine model to the black lens mask gives 26.7
measured.source_method: center that maximizes the variance of the angle-averaged radial profile
measured.outer_cut_sequence: trough yellow < black < yellow < blue < white < black crest, bins of f at -1.6, -0.8, -0.2, 0.8, 1.4 on a sum in [-2, 2]
measured.near_source_cycle: red 50 %, black 37 %, blue/white line 12 % (phase table at pitch 26.5)

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Six-ink palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The composition is the plate's own (tilted axis, different source gap), so output rects were chosen with search.py over the same patch size; the whole plate and the eye are compared in place.

limits: Benchmark mean 0.89. Tone histograms (0.70 to 0.85) miss because the reference is a soft, upscaled JPEG whose 3 px edge ramps put 15 to 20 % of every patch in mid-tones; the plate spreads ink 0.6 px and keeps its edges, since more spread cost the texture spectrum more than it gained.
Ink colors score 0.8 to 0.96 for the same reason: the reference's per-ink class means are pulled toward gray by edge mixes.
The eye patch's contrast (0.26) is JPEG noise in a flat disc, 11 levels of standard deviation; the plate keeps 10 levels of grain, 3 after rounding, instead of chasing it.

Inside the capsule the reference cuts black diamonds with white rims where the two trains are equal; the plate's capsule is dominated by the nearer source in its tilted composition, so those read as rounded blocks.

The reference is warped unevenly (local pitch 25 to 29.5 px); the plate uses a smooth sheet warp and a lens bulge instead, and its ink zones are a parallelism test and a capsule, not the reference's hand-masked shapes.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
